What’s Next · Where is this going?

The next layer of human optimization.

The story is expanding beyond peptides toward tighter connections between therapeutics, biomarkers, diagnostics, wearables, mitochondrial science and personalized decision-making.

Frontiers to watch

Where the story is moving.

We focus on areas where science, access and consumer behavior are changing quickly—not on predicting winners.

Beyond single-pathway drugs.

Multi-agonists, amylin combinations and next-generation metabolic agents are reshaping expectations for obesity and metabolic disease.

From “energy” claims to specific biology.

Mitochondrial targets are moving from wellness shorthand toward more precise questions about disease, aging and adaptation.

Measurement gets more continuous.

More frequent biological data could make intervention decisions more personalized—and more complicated.

Passive data becomes context.

The next generation of devices may matter less as gadgets and more as inputs into broader health decisions.

Repair becomes a research category.

Cell, tissue and signaling approaches remain scientifically important while demanding especially careful evidence boundaries.

Interpretation becomes the bottleneck.

More data does not automatically create better decisions. The next challenge is making evidence understandable and actionable without overclaiming.
